verdicts.title: The logo is a validated asset snapshotted at save, not a URL fetched per render
verdicts.ambition_why: Turns a URL re-fetched on every render into a validated, pinned, sniffed asset read through one entitlement door; closes a TOCTOU the code itself concedes (logo-fetch.ts:22-23, branding.ts:32-33) and the 'DNS-pinned' claim at branding/route.ts:81 that is not true today.
verdicts.grounding_why: Every anchor holds: fetch(url) re-resolves after lookup (logo-fetch.ts:36/44), image/* accepted at :55 while @react-pdf/image isValidFormat admits only jpg/jpeg/png/svg (index.js:186-192) and throws at :226, render(undefined) drops name+accent (pdf/route.ts:112-115) while :122 still names the file after the brand, shareChrome.tsx:21 hotlinks, four planAllowsWhiteLabel call sites, zero logoSnapshot hits in src+prisma.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: 8 cases, all red today (no fetchSafeLogo, no snapshot table, no door, webp passes save-probe); the pinned-lookup case (second queued DNS answer never consumed) is a real discriminator; the 1 h negative cache is asserted only in prose of case 7 and should get its own timer assertion.
verdicts.notes: Floors: L/7/8/6, 14 files + 1 migration, 8 cases, gate architecture (additive cache table, droppable). What is paid for is unchanged: the door applies the same planAllowsWhiteLabel check both deliverables apply today. Risks the builder must hold: init.sql parity test; TEXT not bytea; share page stays <= 300 (291 -> ~286 claimed). Shared surface next.config.ts is EDITED by inspector A (line 100) - sequence after it or leave the CSP comment alone. Not previously proposed (10-05 cards, BACKLOG, log -200: only 267d2a14 'apply stored brand' landed, which this builds on).

verdicts.grounding_why: playbook-adoption.ts:103-107 reads every scan of every adopting repo unbounded with no engineProvider (grep: 0 hits); :138 uses <=; stampLandedPlaybook uses appliedAt @default(now()) (schema:1117) from reconcilePracticeAdoption (practice-adoption.ts:265-266) inside runScanConsequences (scan-consequences.ts:94-96), so the landing scan is the baseline; latestScanAtPerRepo/scanAtBeforePerRepo/atPairs exist (org-rollup-latest-scans.ts:42/53/59); the guard scans src/lib/db with an allowlist and this file is org-*-named-not, so it is outside it. git log on the file shows run-3's door work did not touch it.

The :133 guard is deliberately retitled (same output) - honest.

verdicts.title: Re-roll an edited playbook to the repos still on an older version
verdicts.ambition_why: Closes the playbook half of 'reuse doesn't update': an edited standard can reach its adopters, with a behind/diverged/unversioned classification, a capped admin rollout and a ledger that stays true after the revision lands - the move a principal makes once versions exist but never propagate.
verdicts.grounding_why: write.ts:79-88 409s on any base file; playbook-apply.ts:54 derives the path from the CURRENT title slug; :106 patternVersion null and practices.md:586-587 says playbook rows are not version-tracked; practice-adoption.ts:170-182 refreshes proposedHash on re-propose while reconcile.ts:94-112 compares only adoptedHash/outline (so a landed revision reads as drift); practice-shape.ts:160/203 census covers docs/playbooks with contentDigest; appliedVersion writers are exactly playbooks.ts:212-213 and playbook-adoption.ts:50; PlaybookApplyBatch.tsx:11-13 claims a re-apply re-surfaces the branch.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: 6 cases, red today (re-apply 409s); write.test.ts:126 pinned green for every caller without the option; the rebaseline case needs proposedHash === census hash which no fixture sets. Missing: a case where base bytes match the digest at check time but the PUT carries the base blob sha so a concurrent base edit fails at GitHub - the builder should add it under case 2.
verdicts.notes: RULING on the openDraftPr change: in-scope CONTRACT NARROWING, not a policy-loosen. The invariant the 409 protects is 'never delete content the customer authored' (write.ts:76-81); the option admits a replace only when the base file's bytes are exactly what Ascent itself landed (ledger adoptedHash = contentDigest, the same digest the census computes), it is opt-in, only the revise route passes it, a drifted file fails the digest and is never offered, and the default path and its pinned test are unchanged. Condition: the digest must be computed on the base file's CONTENT fetched at write time (not inferred from existingFileSha) and the PUT must carry that blob sha. Side effect worth naming in practices.md: the rebaseline edge also fixes the same latent drift-after-rollout for house rollouts (practices/rollout re-proposes over adopted rows). Floors: L/8/8/7, 14 files; the line estimate sums to ~900 (slightly over ~800) - acceptable for an L. Not a re-propose: it absorbs the open S item 'show which playbook version a repo adopted' and grows it.

verdicts.title: A scan credit reservation is a keyed ledger object: refund names its debit
verdicts.ambition_why: Gives the fleet reservation an identity (debit scan-job:<job>:<attempt>, refund refund:<debit>) and derives 'does this job hold a credit' from the ledger, retiring a best-effort boolean as the only record of money - the hosted lane already proves the pattern in-repo.
verdicts.grounding_why: credits.ts:154 auto:<uuid> per invocation; :379 scan:<id> | auto:<uuid>; scan-credit.ts:119-127 passes no externalId (grep: 0) and swallows failure; scan-queue-worker.ts:345-349 returns charged regardless, fed into settleJob at :377/:389/:406; import/route.ts:572-574 same; scan-jobs.ts:420 clears creditCharged on creditRefunded, :416-422 best-effort, :440 reaper leaves it; rescan.md:394-397 documents the kill window; hosted-credits.ts:84/138 keyed; registry-map records the deviation.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Each of the 6 money cases names a concrete today-failure (double debit, lost refund erased, double refund minting +2, free scan on a refunded key) and an exact ledger assertion (one -1 row, one +1 row, net 0); the two guards pin reconciliation and plain grants unchanged.
verdicts.notes: RULING on the credits boundary: IN SCOPE as ledger correctness. No price, amount, grant, or charging rule moves - the same scans are charged one credit under the same shouldRefundScan policy; only the externalId values and the truthfulness of 'refunded' change. One behavioural edge to state in rescan.md: case 3 (attempt 1 refunded, settle lost, attempt 2 delivers a real scan) is charged once where today it is served free on a refunded key - that is the stated policy applied correctly, not a new charge. Floors: L/7/8/6, 7 edits + 3 new (~580 lines), 8 cases, gate contract, no schema change. Both callers (scan-queue-worker.ts, import/route.ts) were edited by run-1 and run-2; the cited lines hold on the current tree. heldScanReservation is a prefix read on the unique externalId column - fine. Overlap with credits B only on the db/index.ts barrel.

verdicts.title: Credits shows the fleet scans it skipped, and resumes them in one click
verdicts.ambition_why: Turns a dead-end 'paused' sentence into the backlog it already knows about and a priced resume through the existing route - the surface reports a state and offers its exit.
verdicts.grounding_why: scan-queue-worker.ts:334-338 settleCadence then settleJob skipped 'insufficient credits' (a top-up waits a full cadence); only the push path writes a scan outcome (:327-333); CreditsControl.tsx:139 is a sentence with no count or action; /api/org/scan accepts repos (:80-82) and caps to balance + allowance (:103-111) behind requireOrgAccess (:54); credits GET is requireOrgRead (:16); ScanScope.repos exists (useOrgScanButton.ts:39); immediateScanCredits (WatchCostTail.tsx:23-29); ScanJob has state/settledAt (schema:2972/2986).
verdicts.falsifiability_why: 6 non-guard cases red today with concrete folds (newest-job-per-repo, probe lane and other errors excluded, oldest-first plan of 5 of 7, top-up-first); the route case asserts the requireOrgAccess gate on the field; the click case asserts the exact repos reach POST /api/org/scan.
verdicts.notes: RULING on the credits boundary: IN SCOPE. Nothing about what is charged moves: the resume is the existing /api/org/scan { repos } which reserves one credit per repo beyond the allowance exactly as Scan all does, and the draw is disclosed via immediateScanCredits before the click. Floors: M/6/8/5, 5 edits + 6 new, 7 cases, gate none, additive GET field. LOC: CreditsControl.tsx 200 -> ~212 under src/components (cap 300). No overlap with run-4 write sets; premises rest on run-1-landed files (useOrgScanButton.ts, scanRunRosterModel.ts) at their current lines.

verdicts.title: One public-corpus door: the landing register stops ranking mock floors

Add LeaderboardTable.tsx (177 -> ~150) and RegisterChips.tsx (~70) to the write set.
verdicts.ambition_why: One corpus module (tenancy where + per-row check + rankable predicate derived from BENCHMARK_ELIGIBLE) that both public rankings build on, plus the register's own mock-crowded candidate window fixed - the root the MC-B18/MC-B42 copies were working around.
verdicts.grounding_why: data.ts:6-17 states both invariants; :190 per-row private refusal; :213 verified literal (third copy beside org-rollup.ts:101 isMockScore and eligibility.ts:35 BENCHMARK_ELIGIBLE); :256-262 groupBy _max over ALL scans before the verified split at :306; GALLERY_REPO_SELECT (scans-read.ts:860-883) has neither isPrivate nor engineProvider; :963-964 id-only extra fetch; :979-981 mock-inclusive sort; IndexGallery.tsx:85 'The register'; page.tsx:114 exampleRepos from topAiNative; aboutFleetModel.ts:70 currentRubric-only filter (run-1 about B, landed e7e15ffa).
verdicts.falsifiability_why: 8 cases red today, including the 500-mock-high candidate-window case that only this card covers; the guard case seeds a violation and a comment-only non-violation per AGENTS.md. The private-row case is defence in depth (both gallery windows already pin orgId + isPrivate:false at scans-read.ts:936/952), so its 'today published' wording overstates.
verdicts.notes: RULING: this is the surviving card of the landing-A / portfolio-A pair. Floors after the merge: L/7/8/6, ~14 files, 10 cases, gate policy-tighten (the landing board's ranked set shrinks by mock rows; nothing public widens). Caveat for the builder: isRankableScan must take only the ENGINE half of BENCHMARK_ELIGIBLE - the register chips a stale rubric and does not de-rank it (data.ts:218, LeaderboardTable.tsx:130-131), so deriving the predicate from the whole BENCHMARK_ELIGIBLE object would silently de-rank r10 rows. Three-commit rollback with the scans-read re-export keeping db/index.ts:40 and scans.ts:23 unchanged is sound. Landing B edits IndexGallery.tsx after this.

verdicts.title: DEV_INSPECT gets one definition with its production floor; dev surfaces pinned
verdicts.ambition_why: Applies the house escape-hatch rule to the one flag that lacks it and pins three dev-surface gates with comment-stripped, seeded guards - correct and cheap, but a hardening, not a design move.
verdicts.grounding_why: next.config.ts:100 registers the loader on DEV_INSPECT === '1' alone while :98-99 claims production is unaffected; source-loc-loader.cjs:29 re-reads the raw string; build is next build (package.json:16); layout.tsx:80 is a call-site mount check; env.ts:112-115/125-128/226-229 carry the floor inside the definition; all four seed routes gate first (verified: seedRequestAuthorized is the first statement in each POST) but only seed-auth.test.ts and a mock assert it; seed-ai-usage/route.ts is tracked and absent from context-map.json:499-513.
verdicts.falsifiability_why: Cases 1-4 are red today (no definition; loader stamps and config registers under NODE_ENV=production + DEV_INSPECT=1); the three guards are green-before by design but each seeds a violation and a prose-only non-violation, per the AGENTS.md rule for source-scanning gates.
verdicts.notes: CONFIRMED: the production floor lives inside the flag's own definition - devInspectEnabled(env = process.env) returns false on env.NODE_ENV === 'production' BEFORE reading DEV_INSPECT, and both readers (next.config.ts, the Turbopack loader) call it instead of the raw string; the guard then forbids any other raw read. next build sets NODE_ENV=production before loading next.config, so the floor bites at config time. Builder note: next.config.ts is TS/ESM - import the .cjs via createRequire or a relative import that the Next config loader accepts; keep the .cjs dependency-free so the loader can require it. Floors: M/5/7/4, 3 edits + 3 new, 7 cases, gate policy-tighten. Overlaps branding A on next.config.ts (branding A lists it as a shared surface for the CSP comment at :10-11; this card edits :100) - sequence or keep edits disjoint.

No overlap with any other card or run-4 write set.
